To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dark matter fraction within the inner 2 kpc is constant along the evolutionary paths of early type galaxies and increases with redshift, while the dark matter slope is close to that predicted by a NFW profile, but is poorly constrained.

(i) the average dark matter mass profile of massive early type lenses is close to a Navarro F Frenk White (NFW) profile; (ii) the dark matter mass is higher in lenses with higher redshift and in lenses with lower stellar mass density; (iii) the dark matter slope is not well constrained by lensing; (iv) the IMF is close to a Chabrier IMF at log M >11.5 and increases with increasing stellar mass density; and
the average stellar IMF normalization is a strong function of stellar mass density but does not depend on stellar mass or redshift.

the dark matter halos of massive early type lenses are more concentrated than their stars, and that the IMF of the stars is close to a universal Salpeter IMF, but with a normalization that scales with stellar mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dark matter fraction in massive galaxies is constant with redshift and that the IMF of massive galaxies is consistent with a Salpeter-like IMF at log M ~ 11.5.
the internal structure of early type galaxies is well described by the classical model of dissipationless collapse and that the IMF of massive early types is consistent with a Salpeter law.

the dark matter fraction is roughly constant in the inner 5kpc of early type galaxies, while the IMF normalization is correlated with stellar mass and independent of dark matter halo properties and redshift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dark matter content of the inner regions of massive early type galaxy halos does not change significantly over the past 7 Gyr, while the stellar mass increases by a factor of 3-4.
the internal structure of early type galaxies does not evolve with cosmic time.
the stellar mass density is the main driver of the evolution of massive early type galaxy structure, while the IMF is a secondary parameter.
